item.content:encoded:
Years later, it occurs to me that launching -1 into the sun would be just as bad an idea as dropping it into scp-blackbox. It seems to be only as durable as regular iron, so it would burn up utterly and so goes Darkman's cell door.

But launching -1 into an orbit that keeps it on the opposite side of the sun from Earth; that seems like a safer, cheaper, and practically permanent containment solution. After all, that's basically what Lite-Brite did in the first place.
Fringe benefit, no constant seep of radiation from atmosphere colliding with the stationary -2.

item.content:encoded:
This is one of those SCPs that is really good about blending the High Science and High Myth aspects of ancient objects of incredible power. It's like finding a superhero movie that balances the right amounts of in-costume and out-of-costume moments… it's very rare and when you find one you enjoy the hell out of it.

Also for some reason I can't help but be amused by the idea of the Foundation deciding that since they were attempting to contain an SCP, the remaining members of the tribe count as a precursor group and they roll them in. Picturing this weatherbeaten old dude with his scraggly white beard and gleaming bald head, total stereotype of the grizzled ancient islander, except he's wearing a suit and doing paperwork related to replacing the bulbs in SCP-435's containment.

"Majoombi! Bring me Form 435-R-1! This one was photocopied badly!"
